_meta.description: IP102 is a large-scale benchmark dataset for insect pest recognition with 102 classes. This file maps every class to a farmer-friendly common name, description, affected crops, symptoms, organic & chemical control measures, and prevention tips.
_meta.note: When the AI returns a scientific class name, the frontend looks it up here and shows the friendly_name first.

fallback.description: We were unable to confidently match this image to a pest in our library. Please try a clearer photo, or seek advice from an agricultural expert.
fallback.organic_control: Maintain field hygiene, remove weeds, and inspect crops regularly. Consult an agronomist for tailored advice.
fallback.chemical_control: Do not apply chemicals without expert identification — wrong pesticides can damage crops and harm beneficial insects.
fallback.prevention: Practice crop rotation, plant resistant varieties, and monitor fields at least twice weekly during the growing season.

rice leaf roller.description: A common rice pest whose larvae roll rice leaves into tubes and feed inside, leaving white streaks visible from a distance.
rice leaf roller.symptoms: Rolled or folded leaves with white longitudinal streaks; scraped leaf surfaces; reduced grain filling.
rice leaf roller.organic_control: Release Trichogramma egg parasitoids; spray neem oil; encourage spiders and dragonflies in paddies; flood and drain to disturb larvae.
rice leaf roller.chemical_control: Apply chlorantraniliprole or flubendiamide at the early larval stage; rotate insecticide groups to prevent resistance.
rice leaf roller.prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen fertiliser; plant resistant rice varieties; synchronise planting dates within a community.

rice leaf caterpillar.description: Caterpillars that chew large irregular holes through rice leaves, reducing the photosynthetic area of the plant.
rice leaf caterpillar.symptoms: Ragged, holed leaves; defoliation in heavy infestations; visible green-brown caterpillars feeding at night.
rice leaf caterpillar.organic_control: Use Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) sprays; hand-pick larvae in small plots; conserve natural enemies like spiders and dragonflies.
rice leaf caterpillar.chemical_control: Spray emamectin benzoate or spinosad targeting young larvae; apply in the evening.
rice leaf caterpillar.prevention: Keep bunds and field edges clean of weeds; avoid late planting outside the synchronised window.

paddy stem maggot.description: A fly whose larvae tunnel inside rice stems, killing the central shoot and producing characteristic 'deadhearts'.
paddy stem maggot.symptoms: Yellow, drying central shoots that pull out easily (deadheart); reduced tillering; stunted plants.
paddy stem maggot.organic_control: Encourage natural parasitoid wasps; drain water periodically to disturb life cycle; remove and destroy affected tillers.
paddy stem maggot.chemical_control: Apply cartap hydrochloride or fipronil granules at transplanting; foliar spray with thiamethoxam if infestation appears.
paddy stem maggot.prevention: Use resistant varieties; avoid staggered planting; plough fields after harvest to expose pupae.

asiatic rice borer.description: Larvae bore into rice stems and feed inside, causing deadhearts in young plants and whiteheads in mature ones.
asiatic rice borer.symptoms: Deadheart (dead central shoot); whitehead (empty panicles); small entry holes on stems with frass.
asiatic rice borer.organic_control: Release Trichogramma egg parasitoids; use light traps to catch adult moths; remove and burn stubble after harvest.
asiatic rice borer.chemical_control: Granular cartap or fipronil at peak egg-laying; chlorantraniliprole spray for young larvae.
asiatic rice borer.prevention: Plough under and destroy stubble; synchronise planting; use resistant varieties; avoid excess nitrogen.

yellow rice borer.description: Yellow moths whose larvae bore into rice tillers; one of the most destructive rice stem borers in Asia.
yellow rice borer.symptoms: Deadhearts in vegetative stage; whiteheads at panicle stage; moths visible at night near lights.
yellow rice borer.organic_control: Release Trichogramma japonicum; install pheromone traps; flood fields after harvest to drown pupae.
yellow rice borer.chemical_control: Chlorantraniliprole, cartap, or fipronil at early larval stage; rotate active ingredients.
yellow rice borer.prevention: Plough fields right after harvest; remove alternate host grasses; synchronise community planting dates.

rice gall midge.description: A tiny fly whose larvae cause the central shoot of rice tillers to form a hollow tubular 'silver shoot' or onion leaf.
rice gall midge.symptoms: Tubular silver shoots replacing leaves; affected tillers do not produce panicles; excess tillering.
rice gall midge.organic_control: Avoid late planting; plough infested stubble; conserve parasitoid Platygaster oryzae.
rice gall midge.chemical_control: Apply carbofuran or fipronil granules in standing water; foliar spray with chlorpyrifos if needed.
rice gall midge.prevention: Use resistant varieties (e.g. IR36, IR64); plant within recommended sowing window.

rice stemfly.description: Larvae bore into the developing rice tiller, distorting growth and reducing panicle formation.
rice stemfly.symptoms: Twisted or distorted shoots; reduced panicle emergence; thin tillers.
rice stemfly.organic_control: Encourage natural enemies; use light traps; remove infested tillers from nursery.
rice stemfly.chemical_control: Systemic insecticides like imidacloprid or thiamethoxam at nursery stage.
rice stemfly.prevention: Use clean nursery stock; avoid waterlogging young transplants; rotate with non-host crops.

brown plant hopper.description: Sap-sucking hoppers that cluster at the base of rice plants. Heavy infestations cause 'hopperburn' — circular patches of dried, dead rice.
brown plant hopper.symptoms: Yellowing then drying of plants in circular patches (hopperburn); honeydew and sooty mould; transmits rice viruses.
brown plant hopper.organic_control: Drain field periodically; release mirid bugs (Cyrtorhinus lividipennis); avoid broad-spectrum sprays that kill natural enemies.
brown plant hopper.chemical_control: Buprofezin or pymetrozine; avoid overuse of pyrethroids which can cause resurgence.
brown plant hopper.prevention: Use resistant varieties; avoid excess nitrogen; maintain proper plant spacing for ventilation.

white backed plant hopper.description: A planthopper distinguished by a white stripe on its back. Sucks rice sap and transmits virus diseases.
white backed plant hopper.symptoms: Yellowing leaves; stunted growth; honeydew; transmits Rice Black-Streaked Dwarf Virus.
white backed plant hopper.organic_control: Encourage spiders and mirid predators; drain fields; remove weeds that host the pest.
white backed plant hopper.chemical_control: Buprofezin at nymph stage; thiamethoxam or dinotefuran for adults.
white backed plant hopper.prevention: Plant resistant varieties; avoid dense planting; rogue infected plants early.

small brown plant hopper.description: A small brown hopper that transmits dangerous rice virus diseases including stripe virus.
small brown plant hopper.symptoms: Stunting and yellowing; viral disease symptoms; sticky honeydew on lower leaves.
small brown plant hopper.organic_control: Conserve natural enemies; remove grass weeds around fields; use yellow sticky traps.
small brown plant hopper.chemical_control: Pymetrozine, buprofezin, or imidacloprid; rotate to manage resistance.
small brown plant hopper.prevention: Avoid planting near infected wheat fields; use certified seed; resistant varieties.

rice water weevil.description: Adults feed on rice leaves, but the more damaging larvae feed on submerged roots, weakening plants.
rice water weevil.symptoms: Longitudinal feeding scars on leaves; weak plants that lodge; reduced root mass.
rice water weevil.organic_control: Drain field briefly to expose larvae; encourage predatory beetles; delay flooding after transplant.
rice water weevil.chemical_control: Lambda-cyhalothrin or fipronil; seed treatment with thiamethoxam.
rice water weevil.prevention: Delayed flooding; rotate with dry crops; clean equipment between fields.

rice leafhopper.description: Bright green leafhoppers that suck rice sap and transmit Rice Tungro Virus — one of the most damaging rice diseases.
rice leafhopper.symptoms: Yellow-orange discolouration; stunting; severely reduced tillering from tungro infection.
rice leafhopper.organic_control: Use yellow sticky traps; conserve mirid bug predators; remove tungro-infected plants immediately.
rice leafhopper.chemical_control: Imidacloprid or thiamethoxam early in season; do not over-apply.
rice leafhopper.prevention: Plant resistant varieties; avoid staggered planting; rogue diseased plants.

grain spreader thrips.description: Tiny thrips that feed on developing rice grains, causing chaffy spikelets and reducing yield.
grain spreader thrips.symptoms: Chaffy, empty spikelets; brown streaks on grains; silvery patches on leaf sheaths.
grain spreader thrips.organic_control: Spray neem oil at booting; conserve predatory thrips and mites; use sticky traps.
grain spreader thrips.chemical_control: Lambda-cyhalothrin or spinosad at panicle emergence.
grain spreader thrips.prevention: Avoid late planting; manage weeds within and around fields.

rice shell pest.description: Causes damage to rice husks and developing grains, reducing milling quality.
rice shell pest.symptoms: Discoloured husks; reduced grain weight; downgraded milling quality.
rice shell pest.organic_control: Maintain field hygiene; neem sprays at booting stage.
rice shell pest.prevention: Synchronised planting and harvest; remove ratoon shoots.

grub.description: C-shaped white larvae of scarab beetles that feed on roots of many crops, causing plants to wilt and die.
grub.affected_crops: Maize, groundnut, sugarcane, vegetables, rice nursery
grub.symptoms: Sudden wilting; easily uprooted plants; chewed roots; white C-shaped larvae found in soil.
grub.organic_control: Deep ploughing to expose grubs to predators; flood irrigation; entomopathogenic nematodes; light traps for adults.
grub.chemical_control: Chlorpyrifos or imidacloprid soil drench; seed treatment with thiamethoxam.
grub.prevention: Rotate with non-host crops; remove crop residue; light-trap adult beetles in May–June.

mole cricket.description: Burrowing crickets that tunnel through soil, cutting roots and seedlings of many crops.
mole cricket.affected_crops: Maize, vegetables, lawn grass, rice seedlings
mole cricket.symptoms: Raised soil tunnels; cut-off seedlings; uprooted young plants; visible in fresh tunnels at dawn.
mole cricket.organic_control: Soap-water flood in tunnels brings them up; encourage poultry to feed; trap with kerosene-water buckets.
mole cricket.chemical_control: Bait with carbaryl-bran-molasses; chlorpyrifos soil treatment in heavily infested fields.
mole cricket.prevention: Keep field clean of debris; flood-irrigate periodically; encourage birds and toads.

wireworm.description: Slender, hard-bodied larvae that live in soil and bore into roots, tubers and germinating seeds.
wireworm.affected_crops: Maize, potato, sweet potato, vegetables, cereals
wireworm.symptoms: Poor germination; tunnels in tubers; weak, yellowed seedlings; visible orange-brown larvae in soil.
wireworm.organic_control: Crop rotation with brassicas; bait traps with potato slices; deep ploughing.
wireworm.chemical_control: Seed treatment with imidacloprid or thiamethoxam; fipronil soil application before planting.
wireworm.prevention: Avoid planting after long fallow or grass cover; rotate; test soil for wireworm populations.

white margined moth.description: Hairy caterpillars (called Bihar hairy caterpillar) that defoliate many crops in large numbers.
white margined moth.symptoms: Skeletonised leaves; gregarious hairy caterpillars in early stages; large defoliation patches.
white margined moth.organic_control: Hand-pick egg masses and young larvae; install light traps; apply Bt or neem on small caterpillars.
white margined moth.chemical_control: Quinalphos, chlorpyrifos, or emamectin benzoate when larvae are young.
white margined moth.prevention: Plough fields to destroy pupae; remove weeds along bunds; community-level synchronised action.

black cutworm.description: Caterpillars that cut young plants off at the soil line during the night, leaving fallen seedlings.
black cutworm.affected_crops: Maize, vegetables, tobacco, beans, cotton seedlings
black cutworm.symptoms: Seedlings cut at base; missing plant stands; caterpillars hiding under clods or in soil during day.
black cutworm.organic_control: Hand-pick at night with torchlight; bait traps; plough exposure to predators; Bt sprays.
black cutworm.chemical_control: Chlorpyrifos or lambda-cyhalothrin spray on soil at dusk; bait stations with insecticide.
black cutworm.prevention: Clean fields of weeds before planting; deep ploughing two weeks before sowing.

large cutworm.description: Larger species of cutworm with similar habits to the black cutworm but causing heavier per-plant damage.
large cutworm.symptoms: Cut seedlings; large frass pellets; caterpillars up to 5 cm coiled under soil.
large cutworm.organic_control: Light traps for adult moths; encourage ground beetles; soil cultivation.
large cutworm.chemical_control: Chlorpyrifos bait; foliar lambda-cyhalothrin at dusk.
large cutworm.prevention: Avoid planting straight after fallow; rotate with non-host crops.

yellow cutworm.description: Yellow-brown cutworm species that damages seedlings of cereals and vegetables overnight.
yellow cutworm.symptoms: Notched and felled seedlings; ragged leaves on older plants.
yellow cutworm.organic_control: Hand removal; bait traps; promote ground-beetle habitat with cover strips.
yellow cutworm.chemical_control: Chlorpyrifos or cypermethrin at base of plants in the evening.
yellow cutworm.prevention: Clean cultivation; rotation with cereals if previous crop was vegetables.

red spider.description: Tiny red mites that suck sap from leaves, causing yellow stippling, webbing, and eventual leaf drop.
red spider.symptoms: Yellow stippling on upper leaf surface; fine webbing on undersides; leaves drying and dropping.
red spider.organic_control: Strong water sprays on leaf undersides; release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus); neem oil; soap sprays.
red spider.chemical_control: Abamectin, spiromesifen, or bifenazate — avoid repeated use of same group.
red spider.prevention: Avoid water stress (mites thrive in dust and drought); maintain humidity; remove infested plants.

corn borer.description: Caterpillars bore into maize stalks, tassels, and ears, weakening the plant and ruining cobs.
corn borer.symptoms: Holes in stalks and ears; sawdust-like frass; broken tassels; lodging of stalks.
corn borer.organic_control: Release Trichogramma egg parasitoids; Bt corn varieties; remove stubble after harvest.
corn borer.chemical_control: Chlorantraniliprole or emamectin benzoate at egg hatch; granular carbofuran in whorl.
corn borer.prevention: Plough stubble immediately after harvest; synchronise planting; resistant hybrids.

army worm.description: Caterpillars that move in 'armies' across fields, stripping leaves of cereals and grasses overnight.
army worm.affected_crops: Maize, rice, wheat, sorghum, pasture grasses
army worm.symptoms: Sudden severe defoliation in patches; ragged leaves; caterpillars active at night, hiding by day.
army worm.organic_control: Use pheromone traps for monitoring; Bt sprays on small larvae; deep ditches around fields to trap marching larvae.
army worm.chemical_control: Emamectin benzoate, chlorantraniliprole, or spinetoram; spray in the evening; rotate groups.
army worm.prevention: Scout fields weekly; deep ploughing; community-wide synchronised action when outbreak detected.

aphids.description: Tiny soft-bodied insects (green, black, or brown) that cluster on new growth, sucking sap and transmitting viruses.
aphids.affected_crops: Almost all crops — cotton, maize, beans, vegetables, fruit trees, cereals
aphids.symptoms: Curled and yellowing leaves; sticky honeydew with sooty mould; transmitted virus diseases; stunted growth.
aphids.organic_control: Spray strong water jets; introduce ladybird beetles and lacewings; neem oil; insecticidal soap; reflective mulches.
aphids.chemical_control: Imidacloprid, thiamethoxam, or flonicamid; avoid broad-spectrum sprays that kill aphid predators.
aphids.prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen; encourage beneficial insects with flowering strips; remove infested shoots early.

potosiabre vitarsis.description: Adult scarab beetles that feed on ripening fruit and flowers; larvae feed on compost and decaying matter.
potosiabre vitarsis.symptoms: Damaged ripening fruit; beetles visible on fruit clusters in summer; secondary fungal infection of damaged fruit.
potosiabre vitarsis.organic_control: Hand-pick adults at dawn; pheromone traps; bag fruit clusters; remove fallen rotten fruit.
potosiabre vitarsis.chemical_control: Pyrethroid sprays during heavy adult flight; observe pre-harvest interval strictly.
potosiabre vitarsis.prevention: Sanitation — remove decaying organic matter where larvae develop; net high-value crops.

peach borer.description: Larvae bore into peach and other stone fruit, causing internal damage and premature fruit drop.
peach borer.symptoms: Gummy exudate at fruit base; wormy interior of fruit; premature fruit drop; small entry holes.
peach borer.organic_control: Pheromone traps and mating disruption; bag fruits early; destroy fallen fruit.
peach borer.chemical_control: Chlorantraniliprole or emamectin benzoate during egg hatch; multiple sprays may be needed.
peach borer.prevention: Sanitation orchards; prune for airflow; monitor with pheromone traps.

english grain aphid.description: A pinkish-brown aphid that infests cereal crops, especially wheat heads, reducing grain yield and transmitting viruses.
english grain aphid.symptoms: Aphids on flag leaves and ears; sticky honeydew; reduced grain fill; barley yellow dwarf virus symptoms.
english grain aphid.organic_control: Conserve ladybirds and parasitoid wasps; avoid early broad-spectrum sprays; encourage hedgerow habitat.
english grain aphid.chemical_control: Pirimicarb (selective) or pymetrozine — preserve natural enemies.
english grain aphid.prevention: Plant tolerant varieties; later sowing to escape virus vectors; balanced fertilisation.

green bug.description: Yellow-green aphid that injects toxic saliva, killing cereal leaves and transmitting viruses.
green bug.symptoms: Yellow-orange spots on leaves that expand to brown necrosis; leaf death; stunted plants.
green bug.organic_control: Encourage parasitoid wasp Lysiphlebus testaceipes; conserve ladybirds; tolerant varieties.
green bug.chemical_control: Sulfoxaflor or pirimicarb; resistance has been reported in some areas — rotate groups.
green bug.prevention: Plant resistant varieties; avoid stressed monoculture; manage volunteer cereals between seasons.

bird cherry-oataphid.description: Dark olive-green aphid; the primary vector of Barley Yellow Dwarf Virus in cereals.
bird cherry-oataphid.symptoms: Yellow-purple discolouration; stunting; reduced grain set; honeydew with sooty mould.
bird cherry-oataphid.organic_control: Avoid early autumn sowing in BYDV-prone areas; encourage parasitoids and ladybirds.
bird cherry-oataphid.chemical_control: Pirimicarb or pymetrozine when economic thresholds exceeded.
bird cherry-oataphid.prevention: Adjust sowing date; use tolerant varieties; rogue volunteer cereals.

wheat blossom midge.description: Small orange flies whose larvae feed inside wheat florets, shrivelling developing grains.
wheat blossom midge.symptoms: Shrivelled grains; reduced thousand-grain weight; emerging adults visible at ear emergence.
wheat blossom midge.organic_control: Crop rotation with non-host; conserve parasitoid Macroglenes penetrans; ploughing to expose pupae.
wheat blossom midge.chemical_control: Lambda-cyhalothrin at ear emergence if adults are flying.
wheat blossom midge.prevention: Sow resistant varieties; rotate; monitor with pheromone traps.

penthaleus major.description: Tiny black mites with red legs that feed on seedlings, causing silvery leaves and stunting.
penthaleus major.symptoms: Silvery leaf patches; stunted seedlings; mites visible on cool mornings.
penthaleus major.organic_control: Crop rotation; pasture spelling; encourage predatory mites.
penthaleus major.chemical_control: Omethoate or chlorpyrifos at seedling stage if monitoring shows high pressure.
penthaleus major.prevention: Treat seed; spell paddocks; avoid sowing into heavily infested pasture.

longlegged spider mite.description: A spider mite species with characteristically long legs that webs and damages many crops in hot dry weather.
longlegged spider mite.symptoms: Stippling; bronzing of leaves; fine webbing.
longlegged spider mite.organic_control: Predatory mites; water spray; neem oil.
longlegged spider mite.prevention: Maintain humidity around plants; avoid dust; encourage natural enemies.

wheat phloeothrips.description: Slender black thrips that feed inside wheat ears, reducing grain set and quality.
wheat phloeothrips.symptoms: Whitish, bleached glumes; reduced grain set; thrips visible inside florets.
wheat phloeothrips.organic_control: Avoid late sowing; sticky traps; encourage predatory thrips and bugs.
wheat phloeothrips.prevention: Early sowing; resistant varieties where available; rotation.

wheat sawfly.description: Wasp-like adults whose larvae bore inside wheat stems, weakening them and causing lodging.
wheat sawfly.symptoms: Lodged wheat with stems broken near the base; hollow stems with frass inside.
wheat sawfly.organic_control: Solid-stemmed wheat varieties; deep ploughing of stubble; conserve parasitoids.
wheat sawfly.chemical_control: Foliar pyrethroids during adult flight (limited effectiveness once larvae are inside stems).
wheat sawfly.prevention: Use solid-stem cultivars; rotate; destroy stubble after harvest.

cerodonta denticornis.description: Small fly whose larvae mine inside leaves, leaving wandering pale tunnels.
cerodonta denticornis.symptoms: Pale serpentine tunnels in leaves; reduced photosynthesis; weakened plants.
cerodonta denticornis.organic_control: Remove and destroy mined leaves; yellow sticky traps; conserve parasitoid wasps.
cerodonta denticornis.chemical_control: Abamectin or cyromazine — apply when mines are still small.
cerodonta denticornis.prevention: Cover early seedlings; rotate with non-host crops.

beet fly.description: Fly whose larvae mine beet leaves, creating blister-like blotches that turn brown.
beet fly.symptoms: White blister mines that turn brown; defoliation in heavy attacks.
beet fly.organic_control: Cover with insect-proof net; remove affected leaves; rotate.
beet fly.prevention: Avoid planting near previous year's beet fields; remove volunteer plants.

flea beetle.description: Tiny shiny beetles that jump like fleas, chewing many small round holes (shotholes) in leaves.
flea beetle.affected_crops: Cabbage, radish, mustard, canola, brinjal, beet
flea beetle.symptoms: Shothole feeding on leaves; severe damage on seedlings; reduced stand.
flea beetle.organic_control: Cover seedlings with insect netting; yellow sticky traps; kaolin clay; neem.
flea beetle.prevention: Rotate brassicas; transplant strong, larger seedlings; trap crops (radish).

cabbage army worm.description: Caterpillars that bore into cabbage hearts and feed inside, leaving frass and unmarketable heads.
cabbage army worm.symptoms: Holes through cabbage heads; greenish frass; larvae found inside heads.
cabbage army worm.organic_control: Bt sprays on young larvae; hand-pick eggs; pheromone traps.
cabbage army worm.chemical_control: Emamectin benzoate or spinosad; avoid heart sprays close to harvest.
cabbage army worm.prevention: Cover with fine mesh until heading; rotate with non-brassica crops.

beet army worm.description: Polyphagous caterpillars that defoliate many crops and can develop resistance quickly to insecticides.
beet army worm.symptoms: Skeletonised leaves; window-pane feeding by young larvae; frass on leaves.
beet army worm.organic_control: Bt sprays on young larvae; NPV biopesticide; pheromone traps; remove weed hosts.
beet army worm.chemical_control: Emamectin benzoate, chlorantraniliprole, or spinetoram — rotate IRAC groups.
beet army worm.prevention: Synchronised planting; remove weed hosts (pigweed, lambsquarter); deep ploughing.

beet spot flies.description: Fly whose larvae mine beet leaves, creating blister-like spots that ruin foliage quality.
beet spot flies.symptoms: White spotty blisters on leaves; brown patches as mines age.
beet spot flies.organic_control: Remove infested leaves; insect netting; rotation.
beet spot flies.prevention: Clean cultivation; avoid sequential plantings of same crop.

meadow moth.description: Caterpillars that web leaves together and defoliate sugar beet and many vegetable crops.
meadow moth.symptoms: Webbed and skeletonised leaves; large defoliation patches; gregarious young larvae.
meadow moth.organic_control: Bt sprays; pheromone traps; cultivate to disturb pupae.
meadow moth.chemical_control: Chlorantraniliprole or emamectin benzoate; spray young larvae.
meadow moth.prevention: Weed control; rotation; community monitoring during migration years.

beet weevil.description: Large grey weevils that feed on young beet plants in spring, cutting seedlings at the soil line.
beet weevil.symptoms: Cut-off seedlings; chewed leaf edges; weevils visible at base of plants in spring.
beet weevil.organic_control: Trenching around fields; sticky barriers; rotation away from beet.
beet weevil.chemical_control: Imidacloprid seed treatment; pyrethroid foliar spray on emergence.
beet weevil.prevention: Long crop rotation; avoid planting next to last year's beet field; deep ploughing.

sericaorient alismots chulsky.description: Small scarab beetle whose larvae attack roots and adults feed on foliage of various crops.
sericaorient alismots chulsky.symptoms: Yellowing patches in fields; wilted plants; root damage from larvae.
sericaorient alismots chulsky.organic_control: Light traps; entomopathogenic nematodes; deep ploughing.
sericaorient alismots chulsky.chemical_control: Imidacloprid soil treatment; foliar pyrethroids for adults.
sericaorient alismots chulsky.prevention: Rotation; remove crop residues; monitor adult flight.

alfalfa weevil.description: Adult weevils lay eggs in alfalfa stems and larvae feed on leaves, reducing forage quality.
alfalfa weevil.symptoms: Skeletonised and yellow-bronzed alfalfa; small green larvae on leaves; thin first cutting.
alfalfa weevil.organic_control: Early cutting; conserve parasitoid Bathyplectes curculionis; rotation.
alfalfa weevil.chemical_control: Lambda-cyhalothrin or indoxacarb; observe pre-cut intervals.
alfalfa weevil.prevention: Time first cutting to disrupt larvae; encourage natural enemies; tolerant varieties.

flax budworm.description: Caterpillars that feed on flax buds and capsules, reducing seed yield.
flax budworm.symptoms: Holes in capsules; lost buds and flowers; larvae feeding inside capsules.
flax budworm.prevention: Rotation; early-maturing varieties to escape peak moth flight.

alfalfa plant bug.description: Slender greenish-yellow bugs that suck on alfalfa buds and seed pods, reducing seed yield significantly.
alfalfa plant bug.symptoms: Aborted buds and flowers; deformed pods; reduced seed set.
alfalfa plant bug.organic_control: Sweep-net monitoring; early cutting to break cycle.
alfalfa plant bug.chemical_control: Lambda-cyhalothrin or thiamethoxam at bud stage.
alfalfa plant bug.prevention: Manage hedgerows that host bugs; rotation.

tarnished plant bug.description: Small mottled brown bugs that suck plant juices from buds, flowers, and fruit, causing distortion.
tarnished plant bug.affected_crops: Cotton, alfalfa, strawberry, vegetables, fruit trees
tarnished plant bug.symptoms: Aborted flowers and small fruit; 'catfacing' deformities on fruit; pinpoint feeding scars.
tarnished plant bug.organic_control: Sweep nets to monitor; weed control around fields; conserve big-eyed bugs and damsel bugs.
tarnished plant bug.chemical_control: Flonicamid or thiamethoxam; rotate to manage resistance.
tarnished plant bug.prevention: Manage weed reservoirs (especially mullein); maintain ground cover that hosts natural enemies.

Locustoidea.description: Large gregarious grasshoppers that form devastating swarms and strip entire crops bare in days.
Locustoidea.affected_crops: Almost all crops — cereals, vegetables, fruit trees, pasture
Locustoidea.symptoms: Sudden severe defoliation; visible swarms; ragged crop edges; bare stalks remaining.
Locustoidea.organic_control: Beat hopper bands at dawn while cold; deep trenches with kerosene; community action.
Locustoidea.chemical_control: Aerial spraying with malathion, fipronil or IGR (diflubenzuron) by national/regional locust control authorities.
Locustoidea.prevention: Early warning monitoring; report swarms immediately to authorities; community vigilance during outbreak years.

lytta polita.description: Long-bodied black beetles that swarm onto crops and chew leaves and flowers; their body fluid blisters skin.
lytta polita.symptoms: Defoliation in patches; large numbers of black beetles on plants; chewed leaves and flowers.
lytta polita.organic_control: Hand-pick (with gloves — they cause blisters); trap with light at night; cultivation in egg-laying season.
lytta polita.chemical_control: Pyrethroids; spray in early morning when beetles are sluggish.
lytta polita.prevention: Manage grasshopper populations (host of larvae); clean cultivation.

legume blister beetle.description: Striped blister beetles that defoliate legumes and many vegetables in summer.
legume blister beetle.symptoms: Patches of severe defoliation; striped beetles visible feeding gregariously.
legume blister beetle.organic_control: Hand-pick with gloves; row covers; cultivate to disturb egg masses.
legume blister beetle.prevention: Manage grasshopper populations; clean cultivation; spot treatments instead of broadcast.

blister beetle.description: Black-and-yellow striped blister beetles that swarm onto legumes and cucurbits in summer.
blister beetle.symptoms: Skeletonised leaves; chewed flowers; visible swarms.
blister beetle.organic_control: Hand-pick (gloves!); netting; light traps for adults.

therioaphis maculata Buckton.description: Spotted yellow aphids that inject toxic saliva, killing alfalfa leaves and stunting growth.
therioaphis maculata Buckton.symptoms: Yellow then brown leaves; defoliation; stunting; honeydew and sooty mould.
therioaphis maculata Buckton.organic_control: Ladybirds, lacewings, parasitoid wasps; resistant cultivars.
therioaphis maculata Buckton.chemical_control: Pirimicarb or thiamethoxam if thresholds exceeded.
therioaphis maculata Buckton.prevention: Use resistant alfalfa varieties; early cutting; rotation.

odontothrips loti.description: Small thrips that feed on legume flowers, reducing pod set and seed yield.
odontothrips loti.symptoms: Distorted flowers; aborted pods; silvery streaks on petals.
odontothrips loti.organic_control: Sticky traps; conserve predatory bugs and mites.

Thrips.description: Tiny slender insects (1–2 mm) that rasp plant tissue and suck sap, leaving silvery streaks and transmitting Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus.
Thrips.affected_crops: Onion, tomato, pepper, cotton, beans, cabbage, ornamentals
Thrips.symptoms: Silver-grey streaks on leaves; black frass specks; deformed flowers; curled leaves; virus disease symptoms.
Thrips.organic_control: Hang blue or yellow sticky traps near crops. Apply neem oil weekly. Release predatory mites (Amblyseius cucumeris) or minute pirate bugs. Kaolin clay sprays as a deterrent.
Thrips.chemical_control: Use spinosad, spinetoram, or abamectin. Apply early morning or late evening when thrips are active. Ensure thorough coverage of leaf undersides and flowers. Rotate insecticide groups.
Thrips.prevention: Remove weeds and crop residues around fields. Avoid planting near fields with mature thrips. Reflective mulches. Maintain proper irrigation — thrips thrive in dry, dusty conditions.

alfalfa seed chalcid.description: Tiny wasps whose larvae feed inside alfalfa seeds, hollowing them and reducing germination.
alfalfa seed chalcid.symptoms: Hollow seeds; reduced seed weight; emergence holes in seed coats.
alfalfa seed chalcid.organic_control: Early harvest before larvae mature; clean seed; rotation.
alfalfa seed chalcid.chemical_control: Limited options — most reliance is on prevention.
alfalfa seed chalcid.prevention: Clean seed; rotate seed fields; isolate from old alfalfa stands.

wheat wireworm.description: Slender orange-brown larvae of click beetles that destroy germinating wheat seedlings and cereal roots.
wheat wireworm.symptoms: Patchy poor germination; missing rows; weak yellowed plants; visible larvae on close inspection.
wheat wireworm.organic_control: Crop rotation; bait traps; deep ploughing.
wheat wireworm.chemical_control: Seed treatment with imidacloprid or thiamethoxam; fipronil soil treatment.
wheat wireworm.prevention: Avoid planting cereals straight after long grass leys; rotate; monitor with bait traps before planting.

sawfly.description: Adults look like wasps; their caterpillar-like larvae chew leaves, skeletonising them.
sawfly.symptoms: Skeletonised leaves; caterpillar-like larvae with many legs; defoliation in patches.
sawfly.organic_control: Hand-pick larvae; conserve parasitoid wasps and birds; remove infested shoots.
sawfly.prevention: Rotation; healthy plants are more tolerant; encourage birds.

Miridae.description: Large family of small bugs that suck plant juices, causing necrotic spots, blackened buds, and aborted fruit.
Miridae.symptoms: Black sunken spots on shoots; aborted flower buds; misshapen fruit; punctures on stems.
Miridae.organic_control: Sweep-net monitoring; conserve big-eyed bugs and assassin bugs; weed management.
Miridae.chemical_control: Flonicamid or sulfoxaflor; rotate IRAC groups.
Miridae.prevention: Manage weed reservoirs; encourage natural enemies; tolerant varieties.

wheat ground beetle.description: Adults and larvae chew on cereal seedlings and developing kernels; one of the few harmful ground beetles.
wheat ground beetle.symptoms: Chewed seedlings; gnawed kernels in heads; visible black beetles at base of plants.
wheat ground beetle.organic_control: Crop rotation; remove volunteer cereals; cultivation.
wheat ground beetle.chemical_control: Pyrethroids if monitoring shows high pressure; seed treatment.
wheat ground beetle.prevention: Rotate cereals with non-cereals; clean field margins.

wheat blossom midge.description: Another wheat midge species whose larvae shrivel developing grains by feeding inside florets.
wheat blossom midge.symptoms: Shrivelled grains; reduced yield; pale empty glumes.
wheat blossom midge.chemical_control: Lambda-cyhalothrin at flowering during peak adult flight.
wheat blossom midge.prevention: Monitor with pheromone traps; resistant varieties; rotation.

cerodonta denticornis.description: Fly whose larvae create pale wandering tunnels (mines) inside leaves of beet and other crops.
cerodonta denticornis.symptoms: Serpentine pale tunnels in leaves; reduced photosynthesis.
cerodonta denticornis.organic_control: Insect netting; remove mined leaves; conserve parasitoid wasps.
cerodonta denticornis.chemical_control: Abamectin or cyromazine on small mines.

beet leaf miner.description: Tiny flies whose larvae mine inside leaves of many crops, leaving white winding tunnels.
beet leaf miner.affected_crops: Beet, tomato, cucumber, lettuce, peas, ornamentals
beet leaf miner.symptoms: White winding tunnels in leaves; reduced photosynthesis; aesthetic damage on ornamentals.
beet leaf miner.organic_control: Yellow sticky traps; remove and destroy mined leaves; conserve parasitoid wasps; netting.

fruit piercing moth.description: Large moths that pierce ripe fruit with their tough proboscis to feed on juice, causing rot and unmarketable fruit.
fruit piercing moth.affected_crops: Citrus, mango, banana, peach, guava, papaya
fruit piercing moth.symptoms: Small pin-hole on fruit skin; surrounding flesh rots; secondary fungal infection; fruit drops prematurely.
fruit piercing moth.organic_control: Bag valuable fruit; bait traps with fermented fruit and insecticide; net entire trees.
fruit piercing moth.chemical_control: Difficult — sprays don't reach adults effectively. Focus on bait and traps.
fruit piercing moth.prevention: Remove jungle hosts of larvae (e.g. moonseed vine, Tinospora) within orchards; bag fruit.

Erythroneura apicalis.description: Tiny pale leafhoppers that suck on grape leaves, leaving white stippling and reducing vigor.
Erythroneura apicalis.symptoms: White stippled leaves; reduced photosynthesis; honeydew on lower leaves; reduced grape quality.
Erythroneura apicalis.organic_control: Yellow sticky traps; conserve Anagrus parasitoid wasps; remove broadleaf weeds.
Erythroneura apicalis.chemical_control: Imidacloprid or thiamethoxam; pyrethroids for adults — avoid resurgence by preserving natural enemies.
Erythroneura apicalis.prevention: Manage habitat for parasitoid wasps; avoid drought stress; balanced fertilisation.

Papilio xuthus.description: Large green caterpillars of the citrus swallowtail butterfly that chew citrus leaves, especially on young trees.
Papilio xuthus.symptoms: Defoliation of young citrus trees; visible large green caterpillars with eye-spots; damaged growing tips.
Papilio xuthus.organic_control: Hand-pick caterpillars; Bt sprays on small larvae; encourage parasitoid wasps and birds.
Papilio xuthus.chemical_control: Spinosad or chlorantraniliprole on young larvae if numbers are high.
Papilio xuthus.prevention: Tolerate on mature trees (they cause limited damage); netting of nursery trees.

Panonchus citri McGregor.description: Tiny red mites that suck citrus leaf cells, causing silvery stippling and leaf drop.
Panonchus citri McGregor.symptoms: Silver to bronze stippling on upper leaf surface; leaf drop; reduced fruit quality.
Panonchus citri McGregor.organic_control: Horticultural oil sprays; predatory mites; preserve generalist predators by avoiding pyrethroids.
Panonchus citri McGregor.chemical_control: Spirodiclofen, hexythiazox, or abamectin; rotate to prevent resistance.
Panonchus citri McGregor.prevention: Avoid dust; preserve natural enemies; manage water stress.

Phyllocoptes oleiverus ashmead.description: Microscopic mites that cause citrus fruit to develop characteristic bronze 'russet' skin, reducing market grade.
Phyllocoptes oleiverus ashmead.symptoms: Brown-bronze russet patches on fruit; reduced fruit size; rough fruit skin.
Phyllocoptes oleiverus ashmead.organic_control: Sulphur sprays; horticultural oils; preserve predatory mites.
Phyllocoptes oleiverus ashmead.prevention: Monitor with hand lens; spray promptly when threshold exceeded; preserve natural enemies.

Icerya purchasi Maskell.description: Distinctive scale insect with a fluted white egg sac under the body; sucks sap from citrus and many ornamentals.
Icerya purchasi Maskell.symptoms: White cottony egg sacs on twigs; sticky honeydew; sooty mould; weakened branches.
Icerya purchasi Maskell.organic_control: Release vedalia beetle (Rodolia cardinalis) — a classic biological control success; horticultural oils.
Icerya purchasi Maskell.chemical_control: Systemic neonicotinoids if biological control fails — but they harm vedalia beetles.
Icerya purchasi Maskell.prevention: Preserve vedalia beetle by avoiding broad-spectrum sprays; prune infested branches.

Unaspis yanonensis.description: Hard armoured scale insects on citrus that look like tiny shields; weaken trees and cause leaf drop.
Unaspis yanonensis.symptoms: Yellow leaves with scale shields underneath; leaf drop; weakened, dying twigs.
Unaspis yanonensis.organic_control: Encourage parasitoid wasps (Aphytis spp.); horticultural oils during crawler stage.
Unaspis yanonensis.chemical_control: Pyriproxyfen or spirotetramat during crawler stage.
Unaspis yanonensis.prevention: Prune to improve airflow; preserve natural enemies; inspect new nursery stock.

Ceroplastes rubens.description: Reddish wax-covered scales that infest citrus and tropical fruit, producing copious honeydew.
Ceroplastes rubens.symptoms: Red waxy bumps on twigs; honeydew; sooty mould; reduced growth.
Ceroplastes rubens.organic_control: Parasitoid wasps; horticultural oil during crawler stage.
Ceroplastes rubens.chemical_control: Pyriproxyfen at crawler stage; systemic neonicotinoid as last resort.
Ceroplastes rubens.prevention: Avoid bringing in infested nursery stock; preserve natural enemies.

Chrysomphalus aonidum.description: Dark round armoured scale insects on citrus that weaken trees and damage fruit appearance.
Chrysomphalus aonidum.symptoms: Dark round scales on leaves, twigs, and fruit; yellow spots beneath; reduced fruit grade.
Chrysomphalus aonidum.organic_control: Aphytis parasitoids; horticultural oil at crawler stage.
Chrysomphalus aonidum.chemical_control: Spirotetramat or pyriproxyfen at crawler stage.
Chrysomphalus aonidum.prevention: Preserve natural enemies; prune; inspect new stock.

Parlatoria zizyphus Lucus.description: Black armoured scales that produce greasy appearance on citrus fruit, reducing market grade significantly.
Parlatoria zizyphus Lucus.symptoms: Black greasy patches on fruit; reduced market value; yellow leaves.
Parlatoria zizyphus Lucus.organic_control: Parasitoid wasps; oil sprays at crawler stage.
Parlatoria zizyphus Lucus.prevention: Preserve natural enemies; inspect nursery stock carefully.

Nipaecoccus vastalor.description: Round dark blue-grey mealybugs that infest citrus and ornamentals, producing waxy threads and honeydew.
Nipaecoccus vastalor.symptoms: Clusters of dark mealybugs with waxy threads on twigs and fruit; honeydew and sooty mould.
Nipaecoccus vastalor.organic_control: Encourage Cryptolaemus mealybug-destroyer beetle; horticultural oils.
Nipaecoccus vastalor.chemical_control: Spirotetramat or buprofezin; rotate to manage resistance.
Nipaecoccus vastalor.prevention: Avoid ant tending (ants protect mealybugs from predators); preserve natural enemies.

Aleurocanthus spiniferus.description: Spiny black nymphs and white adults that infest citrus, tea, and many ornamentals.
Aleurocanthus spiniferus.symptoms: Black spiny nymphs on leaf undersides; white flying adults; honeydew and sooty mould.
Aleurocanthus spiniferus.organic_control: Parasitoid wasps (Encarsia spp.); preserve natural enemies; oil sprays.
Aleurocanthus spiniferus.chemical_control: Pyriproxyfen or buprofezin at nymph stage.
Aleurocanthus spiniferus.prevention: Inspect imported plants; preserve natural enemies; prune dense canopies.

Tetradacus c Bactrocera minax.description: Large fruit fly whose larvae develop inside citrus fruit, causing rot and complete fruit loss.
Tetradacus c Bactrocera minax.symptoms: Sting marks on fruit; rot and fruit drop; maggots inside; gum-like ooze on fruit surface.
Tetradacus c Bactrocera minax.organic_control: Bait traps with protein and insecticide; bag fruit; destroy fallen fruit; community-wide action.
Tetradacus c Bactrocera minax.chemical_control: Bait sprays with spinosad; cover sprays with malathion at egg-laying time.
Tetradacus c Bactrocera minax.prevention: Sanitation of fallen fruit; bag-and-trap programs; community-wide coordination.

Dacus dorsalis(Hendel).description: One of the world's most damaging fruit flies — lays eggs inside many fruits, causing total rot from within.
Dacus dorsalis(Hendel).affected_crops: Mango, guava, citrus, papaya, banana, tropical fruits
Dacus dorsalis(Hendel).symptoms: Sting marks; soft rotting spots; maggots inside fruit; premature fruit drop.
Dacus dorsalis(Hendel).organic_control: Methyl eugenol traps for male annihilation; bag fruit; sanitation of fallen fruit.
Dacus dorsalis(Hendel).chemical_control: Bait sprays (protein hydrolysate + spinosad); cover sprays if fly populations high.
Dacus dorsalis(Hendel).prevention: Strict sanitation (fallen fruit); area-wide trapping; bag premium fruit.

Bactrocera tsuneonis.description: Fruit fly affecting citrus and stone fruit in East Asia; maggots damage fruit from inside.
Bactrocera tsuneonis.symptoms: Maggoty fruit; sting marks; rotting from within.
Bactrocera tsuneonis.chemical_control: Bait sprays with spinosad; cover sprays.

Prodenia litura.description: Highly polyphagous caterpillars that gregariously feed on many crops; one of the most damaging pests in Asia and Africa.
Prodenia litura.affected_crops: Tobacco, cotton, soybean, vegetables, groundnut, sunflower, maize
Prodenia litura.symptoms: Skeletonised leaves with window-pane feeding by young larvae; defoliation; visible egg masses with hairs.
Prodenia litura.organic_control: Hand-pick egg masses; pheromone traps; NPV biopesticide; Bt sprays on young larvae.
Prodenia litura.chemical_control: Emamectin benzoate, chlorantraniliprole, or spinetoram; resistance develops fast — rotate IRAC groups.
Prodenia litura.prevention: Synchronised planting; deep ploughing; remove weed hosts.

Adristyrannus.description: Planthopper that sucks sugarcane sap and produces massive amounts of honeydew, reducing yield and sugar.
Adristyrannus.symptoms: Yellowing then drying of leaves; copious honeydew with sooty mould; reduced sugar content.
Adristyrannus.organic_control: Release Epiricania melanoleuca (parasitic moth); detrash cane; remove alternate host grasses.
Adristyrannus.chemical_control: Imidacloprid or chlorpyrifos sprays; spot treatments at outbreak hotspots.
Adristyrannus.prevention: Detrashing; community vigilance during outbreak years; resistant varieties.

Phyllocnistis citrella Stainton.description: Tiny moth whose larvae mine inside young citrus leaves, leaving silvery serpentine trails and stunting growth.
Phyllocnistis citrella Stainton.symptoms: Silvery winding tunnels in young leaves; distorted leaves; stunting on young trees.
Phyllocnistis citrella Stainton.organic_control: Conserve parasitoid wasps (Citrostichus phyllocnistoides); preserve natural enemies.
Phyllocnistis citrella Stainton.chemical_control: Imidacloprid soil drench for young trees; abamectin foliar — focus on nursery and young trees only.
Phyllocnistis citrella Stainton.prevention: Don't spray mature trees (tolerable damage); preserve natural enemies; flush growth synchronisation.

Toxoptera citricidus.description: Dark brown aphid; the primary vector of Citrus Tristeza Virus, a devastating citrus disease.
Toxoptera citricidus.symptoms: Aphid colonies on new flush; curled new leaves; Citrus Tristeza Virus quick-decline symptoms.
Toxoptera citricidus.organic_control: Encourage parasitoid wasps and ladybirds; remove ants that protect aphids.
Toxoptera citricidus.chemical_control: Imidacloprid soil drench during flush; foliar pirimicarb.
Toxoptera citricidus.prevention: CTV-tolerant rootstocks; ant management; preserve natural enemies.

Toxoptera aurantii.description: Glossy black aphid that infests citrus and tea flush, also transmits virus diseases.
Toxoptera aurantii.symptoms: Black aphids on new flush; curled leaves; honeydew; reduced flush vigor.
Toxoptera aurantii.chemical_control: Pirimicarb or imidacloprid during heavy flush.
Toxoptera aurantii.prevention: Preserve natural enemies; manage ants; balanced fertilisation.

Aphis citricola Vander Goot.description: Bright green aphid that clusters on young citrus flush, causing leaf curl and reduced growth.
Aphis citricola Vander Goot.symptoms: Green aphids on new shoots; curled and distorted leaves; honeydew.
Aphis citricola Vander Goot.organic_control: Ladybirds, lacewings; water spray; reflective mulches.
Aphis citricola Vander Goot.chemical_control: Pirimicarb (selective); imidacloprid as foliar or soil drench.
Aphis citricola Vander Goot.prevention: Preserve natural enemies; manage ants; balanced nitrogen.

Scirtothrips dorsalis Hood.description: Tiny pale-yellow thrips that rasp young leaves, causing characteristic upward leaf curl and bronze discolouration.
Scirtothrips dorsalis Hood.affected_crops: Chilli, cotton, citrus, tea, mango, vegetables
Scirtothrips dorsalis Hood.symptoms: Upward curling of leaves; bronze 'spider-veining' on leaves; deformed fruit; reduced flowering.
Scirtothrips dorsalis Hood.organic_control: Predatory mites; blue sticky traps; reflective mulches; neem oil.
Scirtothrips dorsalis Hood.prevention: Healthy plants resist better; preserve natural enemies; manage weed hosts.

Dasineura sp.description: Tiny midges whose larvae cause distorted plant tissue (galls), affecting growth and fruit.
Dasineura sp.symptoms: Distorted buds, leaves or fruit; galls visible on tissues.
Dasineura sp.organic_control: Remove and destroy galls; conserve parasitoid wasps.
Dasineura sp.chemical_control: Systemic insecticides at bud-break — but limited effect once galls formed.
Dasineura sp.prevention: Prune out infested tissue; preserve natural enemies.

Lawana imitata Melichar.description: White moth-like planthoppers that suck sap from many tropical crops and ornamentals.
Lawana imitata Melichar.symptoms: White cottony masses on branches; honeydew; sooty mould; weakened shoots.
Lawana imitata Melichar.organic_control: Strong water sprays; preserve natural enemies; pruning.
Lawana imitata Melichar.chemical_control: Pyriproxyfen or buprofezin at nymph stage; neonicotinoids as systemic.
Lawana imitata Melichar.prevention: Avoid dense crowded canopies; preserve natural enemies.

Salurnis marginella Guerr.description: Small planthopper that infests citrus, tea, and many tropical plants, sucking sap from shoots.
Salurnis marginella Guerr.symptoms: White waxy filaments on shoots; honeydew; reduced vigour.
Salurnis marginella Guerr.prevention: Preserve natural enemies; prune dense growth.

Deporaus marginatus Pascoe.description: Small weevil that cuts and rolls young mango leaves to lay eggs inside.
Deporaus marginatus Pascoe.symptoms: Rolled, partially cut young leaves hanging from shoots; reduced flush.
Deporaus marginatus Pascoe.organic_control: Remove and destroy rolled leaves; conserve birds and natural enemies.
Deporaus marginatus Pascoe.chemical_control: Pyrethroid sprays during flush if damage is severe.
Deporaus marginatus Pascoe.prevention: Time pruning to synchronise flushes; clean orchard floor.

Chlumetia transversa.description: Caterpillars that bore into young mango shoots, killing the shoots and damaging the tree shape.
Chlumetia transversa.symptoms: Wilting and dying of young shoots; bore holes with frass; reduced flushing.
Chlumetia transversa.organic_control: Prune and burn infested shoots; pheromone traps; conserve parasitoid wasps.
Chlumetia transversa.chemical_control: Chlorantraniliprole at flush start; emamectin benzoate.
Chlumetia transversa.prevention: Synchronise pruning and flush; remove infested shoots promptly.

Mango flat beak leafhopper.description: Tiny wedge-shaped hoppers that suck sap from mango flowers and shoots, causing flower drop.
Mango flat beak leafhopper.symptoms: Flower drop; honeydew; sooty mould; sticky panicles; reduced fruit set.
Mango flat beak leafhopper.organic_control: Smoke fumigation in flowering; conserve parasitoid wasps; reduce dense canopies.
Mango flat beak leafhopper.chemical_control: Imidacloprid or thiamethoxam during flowering; spray under canopy.
Mango flat beak leafhopper.prevention: Prune for airflow; community-coordinated sprays during flowering.

Rhytidodera bowrinii white.description: Large beetle whose larvae tunnel inside mango stems and major branches, weakening or killing trees.
Rhytidodera bowrinii white.symptoms: Frass at base of trunks; gum exudation; branches drying back; entry holes visible.
Rhytidodera bowrinii white.organic_control: Probe entry holes with wire to kill larvae; seal holes with mud or wax; remove dead wood.
Rhytidodera bowrinii white.chemical_control: Inject chlorpyrifos or imidacloprid into bore holes; pad with cotton soaked in insecticide.
Rhytidodera bowrinii white.prevention: Healthy vigorous trees resist better; sanitation of dead wood; monitor regularly.

Sternochetus frigidus.description: Small weevil whose larvae develop inside mango pulp, ruining fruit and posing a quarantine concern.
Sternochetus frigidus.symptoms: Adults hide in bark crevices; larvae inside fruit pulp not visible from outside; rejected export fruit.
Sternochetus frigidus.organic_control: Sanitation of fallen fruit; bark scraping; bait traps.
Sternochetus frigidus.chemical_control: Cover sprays of malathion or fenthion during fruit set.
Sternochetus frigidus.prevention: Sanitation; pruning to remove hiding places; quarantine inspection.

cnidocampa flavescens walker.description: Bright green caterpillars with stinging hairs that defoliate fruit trees and cause skin irritation to handlers.
cnidocampa flavescens walker.symptoms: Defoliation; visible bright caterpillars; painful stings to handlers.
cnidocampa flavescens walker.organic_control: Hand-pick (with gloves!); Bt sprays on young larvae; encourage birds.
cnidocampa flavescens walker.prevention: Monitor regularly; remove early before stinging hairs develop.

peach fruit moth.description: Caterpillars bore into peach, apple, and other stone fruit, leaving wormy fruit with gummy frass.
peach fruit moth.symptoms: Wormy fruit with frass; gummy ooze at entry; premature fruit drop.
peach fruit moth.organic_control: Pheromone traps; mating disruption; bag fruit; destroy fallen fruit.
peach fruit moth.chemical_control: Chlorantraniliprole or emamectin benzoate during egg-hatch; cover sprays.

Locust.description: Migratory locust — large gregarious grasshopper forming devastating swarms that strip vegetation.
Locust.affected_crops: All crops — cereals, vegetables, fruit trees, pasture, almost any green plant
Locust.symptoms: Sudden severe defoliation; visible swarms covering fields; ragged bare stalks; ground covered in hopper bands.
Locust.organic_control: Trap pits with kerosene; beat hopper bands at dawn while cold; communicate with neighbouring farmers; community action.
Locust.chemical_control: Aerial spraying by national locust control authorities using malathion, fipronil, or IGRs (diflubenzuron).
Locust.prevention: Early warning monitoring of hopper bands; report sightings immediately to authorities; community vigilance during plague years.

small green leafhopper.description: Tiny green leafhoppers that suck sap from tea, fruit trees, and many crops.
small green leafhopper.symptoms: V-shaped browning at leaf tips; rim hopperburn; reduced quality.
small green leafhopper.organic_control: Yellow sticky traps; preserve natural enemies; reflective mulches.
small green leafhopper.prevention: Tolerant varieties; balanced nitrogen; community spraying.

Bollworm.description: One of the world's most destructive pests. Larvae bore into bolls, fruits, pods and ears, causing direct yield loss. Adults are night-flying moths.
Bollworm.affected_crops: Cotton, tomato, maize, sorghum, pigeon pea, chickpea, soybean, sunflower
Bollworm.symptoms: Round entry holes on fruits, bolls, and pods. Frass around holes. Damaged kernels in maize ears. Wilting of flowers and young fruits. Hollowed-out fruits with internal feeding damage.
Bollworm.organic_control: Use pheromone traps for monitoring and mass trapping. Apply Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) on young larvae. Release Trichogramma wasps. Use NPV (Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus) biopesticide. Hand-pick larvae in small plots.
Bollworm.chemical_control: Apply emamectin benzoate, chlorantraniliprole, or indoxacarb when young larvae are present (before they bore into fruits). Spray in the evening. Rotate insecticide groups — bollworm develops resistance quickly.
Bollworm.prevention: Use Bt-cotton or other resistant cultivars. Deep-plough to expose pupae. Maintain refuge crops to support natural enemies. Intercrop with marigold or pigeon pea as trap crops. Synchronise planting dates within a region to break the pest cycle.

Whitefly.description: Tiny, sap-sucking insects with white, powdery wings. They cluster on the underside of leaves, weakening plants and transmitting plant viruses. Adults are about 1–2 mm long.
Whitefly.affected_crops: Tomato, cotton, cabbage, beans, sweet potato, tobacco, cucurbits
Whitefly.symptoms: Yellowing of leaves. Sticky honeydew on leaves and fruits. Sooty mould growth. Stunted plant growth. Wilting. Virus transmission symptoms such as leaf curl.
Whitefly.organic_control: Use yellow sticky traps to monitor and reduce adult populations. Spray neem oil or insecticidal soap on the underside of leaves. Introduce natural predators like Encarsia formosa or ladybird beetles. Maintain reflective mulches to disorient adults.
Whitefly.chemical_control: Apply systemic insecticides such as imidacloprid, acetamiprid, or thiamethoxam. Rotate insecticide classes to prevent resistance. Always follow label instructions and safe pre-harvest intervals.
Whitefly.prevention: Inspect new transplants before planting. Remove weeds that host whiteflies. Practice crop rotation. Use floating row covers on young plants. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilisation which attracts whiteflies.
